what_it_does: This paper describes a chip controller for power-conversion circuits using GaN (Gallium Nitride) transistors, which are faster and more efficient than silicon but also more fragile. The challenge is precisely timing when to turn on and off the transistors to minimize energy waste, and accurately sensing the current without adding extra silicon area. The solution uses a novel technique called gate-charge monitoring—extracting information from the transistor's own control signal—to measure current with less than 1% error, while a special driver circuit provides precise timing without delay.
